edition.volume: The Complete Ascetical Works of St. Alphonsus, Volume XIII: The Holy Mass
edition.accessCaveat: PDF original too large for page-rendering tool here; contents and source passages inspected through independently indexed full-volume transcription and existing short-treatise Wikisource. Printed pages not PDF page indices.

editorialOwnership.dujardin: Only editorial preface meditation §III is Dujardin. It is NOT written by St Alphonsus.
editorialOwnership.alphonsus: The Sacrifice of Jesus Christ, Short Explanation, major practical/ascetical treatises originate with St Alphonsus; verify Grimm additions and later contributors individually.
editorialOwnership.anonymousFrenchAuthor: St Alphonsus expressly acknowledges adapting a learned French author's work; Grimm speculates on Pierre de Condren/derivative published by Quesnel but does NOT conclusively identify original.
editorialOwnership.sourceDistinction: Dujardin's Passion/Salvation-allegory is a voluntary meditation; Alphonsus biblical sacrifice is a theological synthesis; Fortescue is a historical-liturgical external check.

sourceUnits.title: Mass considered in its Relations to the Life of Jesus Christ, to the Ecclesiastical Year, and to the Universal History of Religion
sourceUnits.author: Rev. Léopold J. Dujardin, C.SS.R.
sourceUnits.theme: Mass gestures contemplated as episodes of salvation history, Christ's life and ecclesiastical year
sourceUnits.doNot: Do not assign the text to St Alphonsus or infer historical origin of ceremonies

sourceUnits.title: The Sacrifice of Jesus Christ
sourceUnits.author: St Alphonsus Maria de Liguori
sourceUnits.theme: Four purposes of sacrifice, five characteristics of Old Law victims, fulfilment in Incarnation, Calvary, sacramental Eucharist and heavenly life
sourceUnits.doNot: This adaptation acknowledges an unidentified earlier French author; Grimm raises Condren as a possible underlying source but leaves identity unresolved

sourceUnits.title: Short Explanation of the Prayers of Mass
sourceUnits.author: St Alphonsus Maria de Liguori
sourceUnits.theme: Foot of altar; Introit–Credo; Offertory–Preface; Canon; Pater noster–Communion; thanksgiving
sourceUnits.doNot: Historical dates/assignments must be compared with Fortescue/Jungmann and 1962 wording

sourceUnits.title: Account of a striking miracle: Hosts discovered near Naples (1772)
sourceUnits.author: Editorial addition to Grimm's edition
sourceUnits.editionPosition: Between prayer exposition and ceremonial treatise
sourceUnits.doNot: Not a Scriptural typology, not automatic production miracle claim; individual factual verification required

sourceUnits.title: The Ceremonies of the Mass
sourceUnits.author: St Alphonsus Maria de Liguori, with editor-supplied appendix and notes
sourceUnits.editionPosition: Part II, chapters I–XVII, appendix and related dissertation
sourceUnits.theme: Priest's preparation, celebrant's gestures, rubrical order, Requiem, Communion, ceremony irregularities and nineteenth-century editorial apparatus
sourceUnits.doNot: Not an authoritative 1962 norm; nineteenth-century footnotes/editorial prescriptions differ from 1962

sourceUnits.title: Preparation for Mass and Thanksgiving after It
sourceUnits.author: Compilations of St Alphonsus's works and attributed prayers, with historical contributors
sourceUnits.theme: Before/after Mass, weekly considerations, Passion meditations, before/after Communion and attributed traditional prayers
sourceUnits.doNot: Do not attribute every included prayer to St Alphonsus (e.g. St Thomas, St Bonaventure and St Francis de Sales are named)

sourceUnits.title: The Mass and the Office that are Hurriedly Said
sourceUnits.author: St Alphonsus Maria de Liguori
sourceUnits.theme: Attention, dignity, priestly dispositions and reverent celebration
sourceUnits.doNot: Not a Bible chronology or proof of ceremony origins

publicationConstraints: An original Mass ceremony is not necessarily instituted to dramatize a Bible event; no ritual-history causal claim from Dujardin's analogies.
The Eucharistic Sacrifice makes present the once-for-all offering of Christ sacramentally; do not claim that it repeats all of Scripture or literally re-performs all biblical events.
'Full Bible' means a curated Scripture-horizon reaching from Genesis through Revelation, not a forced link for every biblical book or verse.
Dujardin's dates (e.g. 4000 years) are meditation rhetoric not defensible scientific timeline.
Dujardin's descent to Limbo/Purgatory and remarks about Jesus not being on altar after Communion require Catholic doctrinal and 1962 rubric review before any presentation.
St Alphonsus's eighteenth-century rubrical notes and Grimm's nineteenth-century annotations may not describe 1962 practice.
Edition-aware Latin Vulgate/English Douay/French Crampon links and canonical 1962 prayer IDs required before publish.
Reproduce no full copyright-encumbered modern text; original-source links and attribution maintained; no external navigation substituting for existing Scripture reader.
